parsed_response.reasoning: The finding's factual premise is false: the shared helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse(response, schema)` is designed to accept an app-specific schema, and other apps do the same — the diff shows `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseBody, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema)` in zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts and `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` in office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts. Salesforce defining `salesforceTokenSchema` locally and passing it to the shared helper is the standard pattern, not a divergent hand-maintained parallel path. The claimed drift between sharing/non-sharing paths exists identically in all these apps by design (minimum schema is only used when sharing is enabled), so the finding describes a non-existent inconsistency plus speculative future copying.

judged_text: salesforceTokenSchema is defined locally in CalendarService while every other app relies on parseRefreshTokenResponse's shared minimum schema — a parallel hand-maintained token shape. When Salesforce changes its token response (e.g. adds fields, changes issued_at format), the drift between this schema and the shared minimum schema means the sharing and non-sharing paths validate differently; the next app integrated will copy this local-schema pattern instead of the shared one.

When Salesforce changes its token response (e.g. adds fields, changes issued_at format), the drift between this schema and the shared minimum schema means the sharing and non-sharing paths validate differently; the next app integrated will copy this local-schema pattern instead of the shared one.

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s core claim (“every other app relies on parseRefreshTokenResponse’s shared minimum schema”) is not supported by the diff: multiple integrations pass their own concrete schemas into `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (e.g., Office365 uses `refreshTokenResponseSchema`, Zoom uses `zoomRefreshedTokenSchema`, Google passes `googleCredentialSchema`). `parseRefreshTokenResponse` itself selects the shared `minimumTokenResponseSchema` only when credential sharing is enabled; otherwise it validates against the caller-provided schema. Salesforce adding a local `salesforceTokenSchema` is consistent with this pattern, and the alleged ‘drift’ is speculative rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.
